config.title: Sticky header/footer pattern

intro.title: Sticky header/footer pattern
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a webpage with a header that stays fixed at the top and a footer that stays fixed at the bottom as you scroll, using the sticky positioning pattern. You will learn how to use the CSS 'position: sticky' property to create these persistent elements. The main technologies involved are HTML for structure and CSS for styling and positioning. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to practical layout techniques that enhance user experience on websites.
intro.usecase: Sticky headers and footers are essential for creating intuitive navigation and persistent controls in modern web applications. You'll find sticky headers in e-commerce sites like Amazon, where the search bar and cart remain accessible while scrolling through products. Dashboard interfaces use sticky headers to keep user menus and notifications visible, while sticky footers maintain important actions like 'Submit' buttons on long forms. This pattern improves user experience by keeping critical interface elements accessible without requiring constant scrolling back to the top or bottom of pages.

objectives: Implement a sticky header that remains fixed at the top of the viewport during scrolling
Apply a sticky footer that stays positioned at the bottom of the viewport regardless of content height
Configure CSS position properties to create persistent header and footer elements
Manipulate z-index values to ensure sticky elements overlay page content appropriately
Construct a complete webpage layout using sticky positioning for both header and footer
Update existing static headers and footers to use sticky positioning behavior
Control the scroll behavior of page content while maintaining fixed header and footer elements

steps.title: Add z-index to ensure sticky elements stay above content
steps.instruction: Add a z-index property to both the header and footer CSS rules to ensure they stay above the main content when scrolling.
steps.hint: Set z-index to a positive integer like 1000 for both elements. This creates a stacking context that keeps them visible above other content.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Sticky Header/Footer</title>
  <style>
    /* Add your CSS styles here */
    header {
      /* Make the header sticky */
      position: sticky;
      top: 0;
      z-index: 1000;
    }
    
    footer {
      /* Add sticky footer styles here */
      position: sticky;
      bottom: 0;
      z-index: 1000;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Add your container with header, main, and footer here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: Both header and footer will have z-index: 1000 applied, ensuring they remain visible above the main content when scrolling.
successCriteria: The header and footer CSS rules both contain a z-index property with a positive integer value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added z-index to one element, but both the header and footer need it. Add z-index to the other element too.
steps.feedbackWrong: The z-index property is missing from both header and footer. Add z-index: 1000 to both CSS rules.
